title: Etale locality of the log condition and fine or saturated charts
statement: Let $T$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], with small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and a jointly surjective etale covering $\{T_a\to T\}_{a\in I}$. Let $M$ be a sheaf of commutative monoids on that site (its underlying set presheaf is a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], its sections are commutative monoids and its restrictions preserve multiplication and identity), and let $\alpha:M\to(\mathcal O_T,\cdot)$ be a homomorphism. Use slice-site restrictions [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and the log and chart definitions of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Suppose $(M|_{T_a},\alpha|_{T_a})$ is a log structure for each $a$. Then $\alpha^{-1}(\mathcal O_T^\times)\to\mathcal O_T^\times$ is an isomorphism of monoid sheaves, so $(M,\alpha)$ is a log structure on $T$. Suppose further that for every $a$ there is an etale covering $\{V_{a\lambda}\to T_a\}_{\lambda\in J_a}$ and a chart $P_{a\lambda}\to M|_{V_{a\lambda}}$, where $P_{a\lambda}$ is finitely generated and integral, meaning its canonical map to its group completion is injective. Then the composites $V_{a\lambda}\to T$ cover $T$ and these same maps are charts for $M$; hence $M$ is fine. Charts on a log structure isomorphic over $\mathcal O_{V_{a\lambda}}$ to $M|_{V_{a\lambda}}$ give such charts by composition with the isomorphism to $M|_{V_{a\lambda}}$, with the same chart monoid. If every $P_{a\lambda}$ is also saturated (if $ng\in P_{a\lambda}$ for $g\in P_{a\lambda}^{\rm gp}$ and an integer $n>0$, then $g\in P_{a\lambda}$), $M$ is fine saturated.

proof.text: For every global geometric point t, choose a point in a member U_a of the cover and lift t to s:Spec Omega -> U_a with s composed with U_a -> T equal to t, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. Pointed etale neighbourhoods of s are equivalent to the slice of pointed etale neighbourhoods of t over (U_a,s); the inverse reads an arrow to U_a as an etale U_a-scheme. The forgetful functor from this slice is initial because the pointed-neighbourhood category is cofiltered. Its opposite is final, and Functor.Final.colimitIso gives canonical monoid- and ring-stalk isomorphisms for restriction [def-trf-log-etale-restriction-stalk-comparison], with the same germs [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Their structural maps commute, as is checked on each colimit injection. The local log structure has exactly the restricted prelog data. Transport reflection of units and bijectivity on unit groups through these isomorphisms to obtain the global stalkwise log axioms [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1, printed p. 69 (etale-local fine/fs charts); Expose VIII, Remark 3.3.4(ii) and 3.3.8, printed p. 107 (strict etale chart descent). The local log-unit verification is expanded in the repair report.

proof.text: Construct the global EtaleLogStructure N with underlying prelog structure exactly M and the two proof fields obtained in the first step; no data is selected from an existence theorem. For any etale test W and unit-valued log section m, apply [lem-trf-log-unit-section-lift] to the ring unit represented by alpha(m). Uniqueness identifies all sections over that unit, which gives injectivity of unitSectionMap. Apply the same lemma to any ring unit section to obtain a log section with exactly that image, which gives surjectivity. Pair this sectionwise bijectivity with N and its definitional equality to M.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1, printed p. 69 (etale-local fine/fs charts); Expose VIII, Remark 3.3.4(ii) and 3.3.8, printed p. 107 (strict etale chart descent). The local log-unit verification is expanded in the repair report.

proof.text: For a single chart on N_a identified with M restricted to U_a, fix a geometric point with a lift to V_aj and compose the lift with V_aj -> U_a. The prelog isomorphism induces a monoid-stalk isomorphism by HasColimit.isoOfNatIso. Combine it with the restriction comparisons of step 1. Structural compatibility and uniqueness of log units identify the two unit inclusions. The chart product maps commute with the monoid-stalk isomorphism and the product of identity on P with the ring-units isomorphism. This preserves surjectivity. To compare kernels, use Con.comap_conGen_equiv: the generating relation (p,1)~(1,a) holds precisely when alpha(p)=a, and the ring isomorphism preserves and reflects this equality. Thus the transported section is a chart on the composite test object, with no finiteness assumption. Compose the two covers pointwise [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition]; lift any geometric point through the composite covering [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. The selected chart with the original finite-generation and integrality witnesses gives IsFine [def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum], and the identical witnesses with saturation give IsFineSaturated [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1, printed p. 69 (etale-local fine/fs charts); Expose VIII, Remark 3.3.4(ii) and 3.3.8, printed p. 107 (strict etale chart descent). The local log-unit verification is expanded in the repair report.

proof.text: Finally let $e:N\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_V$ be an isomorphism of log structures over $\mathcal O_V$ and $c:P\to N$ a chart. At a geometric point of $V$, compatibility with $\mathcal O_V$ leaves $\beta:P\to A$ unchanged. The map required in the chart definition [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] for $e\circ c$ is the composite $P\oplus_{\beta^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}N_{\bar v}\xrightarrow{e_{\bar v}}M_{\bar v}$. Both arrows are isomorphisms, the second having inverse induced by $e^{-1}$. Thus $e\circ c$ is a chart with the identical monoid $P$, preserving all three monoid hypotheses.
